rationale: Ownership (selection.json, revision fc9ec3b1, no bundles installed): communication_kernel_sum_ms is generated exclusively by the 13 fp32 c10d::allreduce_ bucket calls of DDP's final-micro-batch reducer (call d0938de87369efd500322679, 12 buckets x 28,351,488 B, and call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b, one 157,541,376 B bucket), all direct children of the single complete-workload project call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0; execution_timeline-1221e205 and nsys-9ed9145c show exactly 13 NCCL kernels and no other NCCL device work. How previous-feedback.txt changes this attempt: trial-5a705e709d excluded communicator rerouting and NCCL env forcing (step 253.9-295.5 ms vs the 144.8 ms limit, rank-1 kernel sums up to 105.3 ms), and trial-43f18a5360 is now attributed by measurement rather than implementation quality: binding_cost-2087a4f7 shows the additive legacy functional binding at the two allreduce_ sites alone costs +92.3/+100.8 ms of clean step time (passthrough 232.3/247.0 vs parent 139.96/146.20), and its added gloo barrier propagated release skew into the remaining 12 launches (rank-0 kernel sums 80.5/73.9/81.1 ms). Both failure classes are therefore avoided structurally: this candidate returns exactly one replacement for the direct project.invoke boundary (zero functional sites, hence zero legacy dispatch tax), performs no barriers, no extra collectives, no comm hook, no environment forcing, no communicator creation, and leaves the DDP reducer, bucket configuration, default NCCL process group and all 13 bucket allreduces untouched. The lever is the only measured, in-contract gap left: collective_calibration-1af5837f puts the warmed intrinsic cost at exactly these sizes at 61.82 ms (rank 0) / 62.90 ms (rank 1) versus baseline samples 63.21/63.32/66.48 and 63.41/63.67/64.12, so the metric (max-rank, median of 3) sits at rank 1's median 63.67 = floor + 0.77 ms, concentrated as mid-burst kernel inflation (seq 26/28/29: +0.25/+0.35/+0.47 ms) and correlated with rank 1's larger comm/compute overlap (20.4 ms vs rank 0's 8.8 ms): the late rank enters the burst with more local compute in flight and more arrival skew, so its NCCL kernels absorb both waiting and SM contention. The replacement re-implements adapter.run with identical semantics - optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) inside the timed boundary, per-micro loss scaling by len(inputs), no_sync accumulation on the first accumulation_steps-1 micro-batches, the synchronized DDP all-reduce on the final backward, one SGD (lr=0.001, foreach=False) step, one final torch.cuda.synchronize, the same result structure - but executes those no_sync micro-batches through the underlying module as CUDA graph replays of the parent's own work: per invocation the static input buffers are copied from the current inputs, gradients accumulate in place into persistent per-parameter buffers that are primed and zeroed before each replay, and the final synchronized micro-batch runs eagerly through the unmodified DDP wrapper whose reducer then sees exactly the same defined non-bucket-view gradients as in the parent (where autograd allocates them per step) and copies them into its buckets before the unchanged 13-bucket all-reduce. Because both ranks then dispatch the pure-compute segments in three near-constant graph launches instead of thousands of Python-dispatched ops, they reach the synchronized backward earlier and more symmetrically, which is expected to shrink the late rank's mid-burst kernel inflation toward its measured floor: max-rank median from 63.67 ms toward ~62.9-63.3 ms (bounded by rank 1's 62.90 ms intrinsic cost), with clean step_ms expected at or below the 139.9-146.2 ms parent range against the 144.8 ms limit since replay removes rather than adds CPU dispatch work. Numerical equivalence is established by construction and verified on two-rank gloo DDP on CPU: adding into zeroed non-view buffers is exactly the parent's steal-then-accumulate arithmetic (0 + x = x in fp32, same kernel sequence, same order), and the full chain - parent first invocation, buffer-primed no_sync segments, eager final micro, SGD step - reproduces the parent's gradients, weights and every micro loss bit-exactly, and matches a serial no-DDP reference bit-exactly, so exact_gradient_replica_check (atol=0.0/rtol=0.0), the global-batch gradient and parameter-update checks and finite loss are unchanged; cross-rank equality is preserved because both ranks run identical deterministic replays and the unchanged NCCL ring on the default group. Honest unknowns to be tested rather than assumed: whether rank 1's +0.77 ms excess is CPU-launch-side (addressable here) or GPU/transport jitter and SM contention no in-contract scheduling change can remove, in which case the run acts as a measured control that pins the in-contract floor; whether graph capture of the no_sync segments composes with the eager final backward without perturbing allocator or timing definitions; and whether parent step-time variance (139.96 vs 146.20 in the AB/BA arms) leaves margin under the 1.05x constraint on noisy runs.

setup_work.build_time: Installation performs no GPU work, no collectives, no parameter or data transformation and allocates nothing: it resolves the project.invoke boundary from context['targets']/'references', validates that the state carries a DDP model, the underlying module, an SGD optimizer and at least two input micro-batches, and returns the single replacement mapping (an empty mapping if any guard fails).
setup_work.capture_timing: Lazy setup inside actual adapter execution, per binding-contract: the first invocation of each worker process runs the pure parent reference (adapter.run), which also completes DDP's one-time bucket rebuild, library warmup and exact outputs; the second invocation - an untimed warmup under the documented harness order (correctness pass, warmup 2, 5 clean timed repeats, 3 separately profiled samples, inventory pass; warmup precedes all timed invocations in every documented order) - allocates the persistent gradient buffers and static inputs, captures one CUDA graph per no_sync micro-batch into one shared pool (torch.cuda.graph performs its documented full synchronize and empty_cache around each capture), then executes that invocation through replays; every later invocation, including the profiled samples and the comm-hook inventory pass, is replay-only. The held-out longer_sequence variant (sequence_length=256, accumulation_steps=2) captures its own shapes in its own worker process; nothing fixture-dependent is cached - each replay reads the current input buffers and the current in-place parameter storage, so the workload executes on every invocation.
setup_work.memory: Setup adds approximately one gradient-sized retained allocation (about 0.5 GB fp32 for GPT-2 124M) held for the process lifetime, static input buffers of a few KiB, and the CUDA graph pool for the captured segments (raises reserved memory; exact size observed at validation). Warm-run peak_allocated_bytes may stay near baseline or fall slightly because the parent's per-step autograd gradient allocations are replaced by the retained buffers - this is a counter/lifetime effect, not a claimed physical-memory saving; framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes and lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes include the capture invocation by definition. If capture fails, the buffers are released and the process degrades to the parent path.
setup_work.state_lifecycle_and_synchronization: reset() reloads weights in place (load_state_dict copies into the same parameter storage the graphs read), gradients are cleared inside the timed invocation exactly as the parent (zero_grad(set_to_none=True), then the primed buffers are zeroed by one fused foreach zero, ~0.5 GB, well under 1 ms), SGD has momentum 0.0 so there is no optimizer state, and the only device synchronization inside the timed step remains the parent's single final torch.cuda.synchronize. No barrier, no extra collective, no comm hook and no environment variable is introduced anywhere, and the gloo control-group barrier in before_run remains outside the replacement. Affected scope is the whole bundle group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb, replaced at its root.
setup_work.route_labels: context['record_route'] is bound with context.get('record_route', ...) and invoked inside the replacement on the chosen path: eager:parent:first_invocation, capture:no_sync_graphs+eager_final_micro, replay:no_sync_graphs+eager_final_micro, and distinct fallback labels separating steady-state, unsupported-signature, capture/setup failure (capture_failed:<Exception>), runtime replay failure (replay_failed:<Exception>) and workload-shape changes.

quality_risks: Capture legality and fallback: if any part of the no_sync forward/backward cannot be captured (uncapturable op, autograd-engine or allocator constraint), the capture exception permanently disables the graph path and routes that and all later invocations through the parent reference (adapter.run) with label fallback:parent:capture_failed:<Exception>; gradients and weights are left in a state the parent's zero_grad(set_to_none=True) fully resets, so the fallback invocation is exactly the parent step. The collective-bearing final micro-batch and the optimizer step are never re-run by a fallback, so a mid-invocation failure cannot desynchronize the two ranks' collectives; even an asymmetric failure (graphs succeed on one rank only) leaves both ranks performing three no_sync micro-batches plus one synchronized final backward with the same 13 allreduces per invocation, so there is no deadlock or collective mismatch by construction.

Accumulation flavor: graph replays require the captured backward to accumulate in place into the primed buffers; this is verified immediately after capture (parameter.grad is buffer for every parameter, else capture aborts with a distinct label) and was verified bit-exact on two-rank gloo DDP on CPU. An out-of-place flavor on CUDA would be caught by this check before any timed invocation uses the graphs.

Numerics: the replacement preserves the exact kernel sequence, order, dtypes, inputs and loss scaling of the parent; adding into zeroed non-view buffers is arithmetically identical to the parent's steal-then-accumulate path (0 + x = x in fp32), and the final synchronized micro-batch presents the reducer the same kind of defined non-bucket-view gradients it sees in the parent, so bucket copies, the 13 fp32 RING SUM allreduces on the default NCCL process group, the reduced gradients and the SGD update are unchanged. Validated bit-exact (gradients, post-step weights, total and per-micro losses) against the parent step and a serial no-DDP reference; exact_gradient_replica_check (atol=0.0/rtol=0.0), global_batch_gradient_check, parameter_update_check, finite_loss and the corruption control are therefore expected to behave exactly as baseline. The captured segment contains no RNG (all dropouts are 0.0) and no collective, so replays are deterministic.

Step-time constraint: replay removes most CPU dispatch work of the first three micro-batches and adds only one fused ~0.5 GB gradient zero plus three small input copies (well under 1 ms) inside the timed region, so clean step_ms is expected at or below the measured parent range (139.96-146.20 ms) against the 144.803 ms limit. Capture is confined to the second invocation, which the documented harness order makes an untimed warmup; the residual risk is an undocumented invocation order that would time the capture invocation, which the request's frozen harness description excludes.

Objective effect is bounded and honestly framed: the transfer itself is measured at its intrinsic floor (62.90 ms max-rank), so the expected improvement is only the launch-skew/overlap component of rank 1's kernel durations (63.67 -> ~62.9-63.3 ms median, about 0.4-0.8 ms). If the residual gap is transport jitter or SM contention insensitive to CPU dispatch scheduling, this candidate reduces to a measured control that empirically pins the in-contract floor; no wire-time reduction or general transfer-speed claim is made - the metric includes device waiting by definition.

Coverage and evidence: CUDA graph replay does not re-run Python dispatch for the captured segment's inner operators; they execute as the same native kernels via graph launches (corroborated by graph-launch entries plus unchanged NCCL kernel counts in runtime traces), while the 13 allreduce_ calls, the final backward and the optimizer step remain eagerly dispatched and traceable. No inner call is eliminated (eliminated_calls is empty) and no consumer changes: the same accumulated gradients feed the same reducer buckets, the same allreduces and the same optimizer. Route labels are candidate self-report, not a substitute for the framework's own output, coverage and trace checks.

Memory reporting: the retained gradient buffers and graph pool increase reserved memory and the lifecycle peak counters; warm-run peak_allocated_bytes may decrease slightly as per-step autograd gradient allocations disappear inside the pool-free path. These are allocator-counter effects under the frozen metric definitions, not the objective and not a claimed physical-memory saving.

No tunable parameters: a single deterministic configuration with an empty parameter_space, so the previous trial's failure mode (search arms on a rerouted communicator producing invalid endpoints) cannot recur.
